title: Jira Support Ticket Template & Required Fields (Escalation Playbook v2)
author: Owen Phillips
content:
## Purpose
This page standardizes **what must be captured in Jira** for Support tickets and escalations so that Support Engineering, SRE/oncall, Runtime, Private Deployments, and Security can act quickly without repeated back-and-forth.

This template is required for:
- All **Sev0/Sev1 (P0/P1)** customer-impacting issues
- Any ticket being escalated to **#eng-oncall / SRE**
- Any ticket where Engineering investigation is requested (even if severity is lower)

## Scope
Applies to Jira projects:
- **SUP-####**: customer-facing Support tickets
- **INT-####**: internal Support tooling/process work (templates, macros, reporting), not customer incidents

For Private/enterprise incidents, follow restricted handling guidance in this doc.

---

## Golden rule: “No metadata, no escalation”
If you need engineering engagement, do not page/DM engineers until the minimum required fields are present (see **Escalation Minimum Bar** below). Exceptions are permitted for active Sev0s where you can start the page while actively filling the ticket, but the minimum bar must be satisfied within **15 minutes**.

---

## Ticket structure (top-to-bottom)
Use the following sections in the ticket description in this order.

### 1) Impact summary (2–4 sentences)
Include:
- What is broken (customer-visible symptom)
- Who is impacted (customer + scope: all traffic vs subset)
- When it started (timestamp + timezone)
- Current status (ongoing / intermittent / recovered)

**Example:**
“Customer reports intermittent streaming disconnects for chat completions in **us-east** starting **2026-02-22 17:10 UTC**. Estimated ~3–8% of streaming responses drop mid-generation. Issue is ongoing; customer has implemented reconnect but sees repeated failures for long outputs.”

### 2) Severity + customer tier
Set these fields at ticket creation and update them as information changes:
- **Severity (Sev0–Sev3)** (per severity matrix page)
- **Customer tier**: Self-serve | Dedicated | Private | Enterprise
- **Escalation required?** Yes/No (set to Yes when requesting engineering)

### 3) Environment + deployment details (required)
Capture:
- **Deployment mode**: Hosted API | Dedicated | Private (VPC/on-prem)
- **Region** (Hosted/Dedicated): e.g., us-east, eu-west
- **Private environment identifier** (Private): cluster name / tenant ID / installation ID (internal only)
- **Model**: exact model name (and variant) used by the customer
- **Model pinning**: pinned version/hash? (Yes/No + value if known)
- **Endpoint**: chat.completions / completions / embeddings / rerank (and any custom route)
- **Runtime/stack version** (if known): runtime build, gateway version, private installer version

### 4) Time window + request identifiers (required)
Provide a bounded time window and IDs. These are non-negotiable for escalation.
- **Time window**: start/end timestamps with timezone (UTC preferred)
- **Request IDs**: at least 3 representative request IDs (more if intermittent)
- **Correlation IDs / Trace IDs** (if available)
- **Org/Project identifiers**: Redwood org ID + project ID (or customer account identifier)

If the customer cannot provide Request IDs:
- Ask for the **response headers** (e.g., x-request-id / traceparent) and a **single example timestamp** per failure.
- If using SDKs, ask for SDK debug logs with request ID enabled (see “Logs to request” below).

### 5) Symptoms + error details
Check all that apply and paste exact snippets:
- HTTP status codes (e.g., **429**, **499**, **500/502/503**, **504**)
- Error message text (copy/paste)
- Client-side exception type (SDK + language)
- For streaming: where it fails (initial connect vs mid-stream), whether a final “[DONE]” is received, and whether disconnect correlates with long outputs
- For timeouts: client timeout vs upstream timeout; configured timeout value

### 6) Reproduction steps (required when feasible)
Provide either:
- Minimal reproducible prompt + params (sanitized), OR
- A reduced test request describing key parameters

Include:
- Prompt size characteristics (short/long), max_tokens, temperature, top_p
- Streaming true/false
- Concurrency level (single request vs burst)
- Whether retries are enabled

If prompts are sensitive, do not paste them. Provide:
- Token counts / length estimates
- Prompt type (classification, extraction, codegen, etc.)
- A synthetic prompt that triggers similar behavior (if validated)

### 7) What changed? (high signal)
Answer at least one:
- Did the customer ship a change? (SDK version, retry policy, timeouts, new region)
- Did Redwood change anything? (known deploy, model rollout, capacity change)
- Has this happened before? Link prior tickets if available.

### 8) Mitigation attempts + current workaround
List what was tried and what helped:
- Backoff/retry adjustments
- Switching region/model (if applicable)
- Disabling streaming / lowering max_tokens
- Dedicated autoscaling changes (if applicable)
- Private networking/SSO config rollback (if applicable)

If a workaround is recommended, link the **Known Issue** page and note whether it is **safe-to-share**.

### 9) Attachments / artifacts
Attach or link:
- Logs (sanitized)
- Screenshots (console errors)
- HAR file (only if approved; treat as restricted)
- Relevant dashboards screenshots/links (internal)

---

## Escalation Minimum Bar (required fields before engaging SRE/Engineering)
Before posting in #eng-oncall / paging, the Jira ticket must contain:
1. Severity + customer tier
2. Deployment mode + region (or private env identifier)
3. Model + endpoint
4. Time window (UTC preferred)
5. At least 3 request IDs (or clear explanation why not possible and what substitute identifiers are provided)
6. Symptoms (status codes/error strings) + whether streaming
7. Customer impact (scope + business impact if known)

**If any are missing:** keep the escalation internal to Support until completed.

---

## Required Jira fields (custom fields)
Populate these in the Jira fields panel (not only in the description). If a field is not applicable, explicitly set it to N/A.

| Field | Required? | Notes / examples |
|---|---:|---|
| Severity (Sev0–Sev3) | Yes | Aligns to Escalation Playbook v2 matrix |
| Customer tier | Yes | Self-serve / Dedicated / Private / Enterprise |
| Deployment mode | Yes | Hosted / Dedicated / Private |
| Region | Yes (Hosted/Dedicated) | us-east / eu-west / etc. |
| Private env identifier | Yes (Private) | Cluster/tenant/install ID (internal) |
| Model | Yes | “redwood-llama-3.1-70b-instruct” (exact) |
| Endpoint | Yes | chat.completions / embeddings / rerank |
| Incident declared? | Conditional | Yes if SRE has opened/linked an incident |
| Escalation required? | Conditional | Yes when engaging engineering |
| Customer org + project | Yes | IDs or canonical customer identifier |
| Time window (start/end) | Yes | Use UTC preferred |
| Request IDs | Yes | Minimum 3 |
| Affected traffic % | Best effort | Provide estimate or “unknown” |
| Workaround available? | Best effort | Link Known Issue if applicable |

---

## Linking conventions (Slack, incidents, GitHub, dashboards)
### Slack threads
- Create a single canonical thread in **#support** (triage) and/or **#incidents** (incident comms) and link it in Jira.
- In the Jira ticket, include:
  - Slack channel name
  - Thread link
  - One-line summary of the latest decision

**Format to paste:**
“Slack: #incidents (thread) – <link>”

### Incident references
If SRE declares an incident:
- Add the **incident ID** and link it in Jira
- Mirror updates per comms alignment guidance
- Do not maintain competing timelines across Slack and Jira; Jira should point to incident timeline for ongoing Sev0/Sev1.

### GitHub pull requests
If an engineer shares a PR or commit:
- Link it under “Development” and also paste in the description with context:
  - PR link
  - What it changes
  - Whether it’s a mitigation or full fix
  - Rollout/verification plan (if known)

### Observability / dashboards
Link internal dashboards where available. Include the exact panel/filters used:
- Region
- Model
- Route/endpoint
- Time window

---

## Logs to request from customers (by scenario)
Only request what is needed. Never request secrets.

### For 429 / throttling
Ask for:
- Full response headers (rate limit headers)
- Timestamped samples
- Concurrency pattern (burst vs steady)
- SDK retry policy configuration (max retries, backoff)

### For timeouts / 5xx
Ask for:
- Request IDs + timestamps
- Client timeout settings
- Whether streaming is enabled
- SDK debug logs for a short window

### For streaming disconnects
Ask for:
- Whether disconnect occurs before first token or mid-stream
- Whether the TCP connection closes cleanly (client logs)
- Any proxy/load balancer in between (customer side)
- Request IDs for both successful and failed streams

### Private (SSO/SAML/audit-log)
Ask for:
- IdP metadata change summary (not full secrets)
- Error codes/screenshots (redacted)
- Private control plane logs (internal collection preferred)

---

## Confidentiality and restricted handling
### When to mark a ticket “restricted”
Set confidentiality to **restricted** (and follow restricted Slack channels if applicable) for:
- Private deployments with customer identifiers, network topology, or security configurations
- Security incidents or suspected compromise
- Any customer-provided logs that may contain tokens, user content, or sensitive IDs

### Redaction rules
- Do not paste API keys, bearer tokens, cookies, SAML assertions, private cert material, or customer PII.
- If you must include a snippet, redact with “<REDACTED>” and state what was removed.

## Quality checklist (Support Engineer self-check)
Before escalating, confirm:
- I can answer “what, where, when, who, how bad” in under 60 seconds from the ticket.
- Request IDs and time window are present.
- I included both failures and successes when the issue is intermittent.
- I captured model + endpoint + streaming setting.
- I linked the canonical Slack thread and any incident reference.
- If Private/security-related, ticket is marked restricted and content is redacted.

---

## Automation notes (incident-bot + required fields lint)
We are rolling out:
- **Required fields lint/checklist** in Support workflow (see ENG-2842)
- **Incident-bot Support Escalation prompts** that collect the minimum bar and post a reminder to link Jira + severity + request IDs (see ENG-2843)

If the automation disagrees with your severity/escalation decision, use human judgment, but leave a comment stating why (e.g., “customer reports full outage but request IDs pending; paging SRE now; will update ticket in 10 min”).
